newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products tiptoe higher in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products tiptoe higher in quiet market.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products edged quietly up about $1 a tonne on Wednesday, traders said.
Gasoline prices were slightly firmer with East Med and West African demand proping up a thin European market, while stronger U.S. markets provided a focus for arbitrage.
Eurograde cargoes firmed $1 to $206 a tonne cif.
NYMEX unleaded firmed by over one cent a gallon following a bullish API report on U.S. demand. Traders said this may stir fresh aribitrage interest.
Naphtha held steady, latching onto the bullish undertone of gasoline.
But European demand remained thin and only interest in shipping material to the Far East was underpinning the market.
Cargoes were assessed notionally around $172/$174 cif Med.

Gas oil started to look long with demand for the previously sought after 1.0 pct and 0.5 pct heating now diminishing. Traders said the latest IOC tender looked fully covered from the Gulf and premiums for 1.0 and 0.5 pct may ease from high fob quotes +$3-3.50. Futures closed $1.00 higher.
The Turkish tender to buy two 25,000 tonne cargoes (18-20, 26-28 dates) was unlikely to boost prices. The tender closes on Friday.
Black Sea 0.2 pct levels were around fob high quotes +$2-2.50 with cif not talked because of poor demand.
Interest for 0.05 has been expressed from NWE with levels put at about high fob EN590 quotes +$3-3.50.
Heavy fuel got a modest $1 a tonne lift from Rotterdam but dealers said the market was still well offered.
Prompt high sulphur cargoes were pegged around $77 fob Italy although a recent bout of demand appears to have been quietly sated. Low sulphur was quiet and held steady $96 cif Italy.
